name: Getuk
description: Mashed cassava sweetened with sugar and colored with pandan or pink food coloring, shaped and sprinkled with coconut.
ingredients: a handful of fresh cilantro, chopped
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with coconut oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the fried shallot crackers (krupuk) and palm sugar until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the roasted peanuts with the tamarind water until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 20 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
Garnish with Thai basil or a dusting of kecap manis (sweet soy sauce).
tips: Bring your roasted peanuts to room temperature before mixing for a smoother, more even texture.
This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
Resist opening the oven door too early — a sudden change in temperature can cause the dessert to sink or crack.
